title: Gale-Shapley Theorem (Existence of Stable Matching)
body_html:
Gale-Shapley Theorem

Theorem. Every finite one-to-one matching market $(M, W, \succ)$ admits a stable matching. Specifically, the matching output by the men-proposing deferred-acceptance algorithm ([[gale_shapley_algorithm]]) is stable.
proof_html:
Sketch

Run the men-proposing algorithm to completion (termination is guaranteed by the proposal-count argument).

Let $\mu$ be the output matching. We verify the two stability conditions:

Individual rationality. A man $i$ only ever proposes to women he finds acceptable (the algorithm consults his preference list). A woman $j$ only ever holds offers from men she finds acceptable (she rejects unacceptable proposers). Hence every matched pair is mutually acceptable.

No blocking pair. Suppose toward contradiction that $(i, j)$ blocks $\mu$, i.e., $j \succ_i \mu(i)$ and $i \succ_j \mu^{-1}(j)$.

Since $j \succ_i \mu(i)$, woman $j$ ranks higher than $\mu(i)$ on man $i$'s list, so $i$ must have proposed to $j$ at some round (before settling for $\mu(i)$ or staying unmatched). At the round $i$ proposed to $j$:

  • Either $j$ rejected $i$, in which case $j$ was holding (or later switched to) some man $i'$ with $i' \succ_j i$, OR
  • $j$ accepted $i$ but was later replaced by some $i' \succ_j i$.

In either case, $j$'s holding partner only ever improves (the algorithm has "no-going-back" monotonicity on the receiving side). So $\mu^{-1}(j) \succeq_j i'$ for the rejecting/replacing $i'$, hence $\mu^{-1}(j) \succ_j i$ — contradicting $i \succ_j \mu^{-1}(j)$.

Lean Status

Statement is at EconCSLib.MarketDesign.Matching.GaleShapley.galeShapley_isStable with a current sorry. Closing this proof is tracked by MT-L1 (#203). The two missing pieces are:

  1. The "monotone holding" invariant holding_rank_mono_run: a woman's holding partner can only improve over time.
  2. The "no free men at termination" property finalState_no_free_men (combined with the proposal-set tracking).

Both follow from straightforward induction on the algorithm's run.

References

  • [MSZ Ch.22, Thm 22.7] Maschler, Solan, Zamir, Game Theory.
  • Gale & Shapley (1962).
